front.title: The ELP8 Container Format for Geometric Wheel-8 Compression, Hash-Anchored Self-Alignment, and Multi-Gear Streaming

abstract.t: This document specifies the binary container format .elp8 (EULNO Layered Protocol 8) for streaming data compression based on counter-rotating modulo-8 wheel geometry, inward-mirror stream bisection, and hash-anchored phase alignment. Unlike conventional archive formats that treat checksums solely as passive post-decompression checks, .elp8 embeds an active Anchor Hash (SHA-256 or SHA-512) inside a variable-tier header (56, 88, or 152 bytes) to deterministically seed wheel sector alignment and enforce constant-time cryptographic self-validation across arbitrary stream sizes up to 2^64 - 1 bytes.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Conventional compression containers append a checksum merely to detect bit errors after decoding completes. The ELP8 (EULNO Layered Protocol 8) format couples the cryptographic digest of the uncompressed stream directly to its geometric phase alignment. By deriving the starting spoke S_0 on an M-spoke modular wheel from the Anchor Hash, encoders and decoders share a deterministic geometric reference point without transmitting external phase tables.

section.name: Conventions and Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 (RFC 2119 and RFC 8174) when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
All multi-byte integer fields in the ELP8 header and chunk frames are encoded in network byte order (big-endian).

section.name: ELP8 Binary Container Layout
section.t: Every compliant .elp8 stream MUST begin with a 24-byte Base Header followed by the Anchor Hash (32 or 64 bytes) and an optional 64-byte Origin Authentication Tag, resulting in a total header length of 56, 88, or 152 bytes.

dl.dd: MUST be the exact ASCII sequence "ELP8" (0x45 0x4C 0x50 0x38).
MUST be set to 0x01 for this specification.

Bit 0 (0x01): Counter-Rotating Wheel Mode (1 = active). Bit 1 (0x02): Inward-Mirror-Split (1 = left half [0..mid-1] advances clockwise; right half [mid..n-1] advances counter-clockwise inward from n-1 to mid). Bit 2 (0x04): Multi-Chunk Gear Mode (1 = framed chunk stream using Gears G0..G6). Bit 3 (0x08): Authenticated Origin (1 = 64-byte HMAC-SHA512 / Ed25519 tag present immediately following Anchor Hash). Bits 4-7: Reserved; encoders MUST set to 0 and decoders MUST ignore.
Modular spoke count (1..255). Default MUST be 0x08. Value 0x00 MUST be rejected.
0x01 = SHA-256 (32-byte Anchor Hash); 0x02 = SHA-512 (64-byte Anchor Hash).
Unsigned 64-bit integer specifying exact uncompressed byte length.
Unsigned 64-bit integer specifying exact byte length of the Compressed Payload.

section.name: Hash-Anchored Alignment and Multi-Chunk Gear Framing
section.t: Prior to geometric encoding, the encoder computes the Anchor Hash H_0 over the uncompressed input stream and derives the root wheel sector: S_0 = uint64(H_0[0..7]) mod M.

When Flag Bit 2 (0x04) is set, the Compressed Payload begins with a 32-bit unsigned integer num_chunks, followed by num_chunks sequential frames. Each frame starts with a 9-byte header: [Gear ID (1 byte)][Chunk Original Size (uint32)][Chunk Compressed Size (uint32)]. For chunk index i (0-based), the local phase anchor is S_i = (S_0 + i) mod M:

ul.li: Gear 0x00 (G0 - Raw Store): Uncompressed chunk bytes (prevents expansion on high-entropy data).
Gear 0x01 (G1 - Deflate): RFC 1951 compressed chunk bytes.
Gear 0x06 (G6 - Wheel-8 Inward-Mirror Spiral): Modular phase-XOR and delta residual stream anchored at S_i, followed by RFC 1951 compression.

section.t: During decoding, the decoder MUST reconstruct all chunks, verify that total decoded bytes equal Original Size, recompute H_1 over the reconstructed stream, and verify H_1 == H_0 in constant time before releasing output bytes.

ol.li: Bounded Decompression (Decompression Bomb Defense): Each chunk MUST NOT exceed 64 MiB (67,108,864 bytes). Decoders MUST enforce bounded streaming decompression and abort immediately if decompressed output exceeds Chunk Original Size.

Source-Side TOCTOU and Symlink Defense: Encoders SHOULD open input files with symlink traversal disabled (e.g., O_NOFOLLOW) and MUST verify via a second-pass digest that the source stream was not altered during encoding.

Atomic Quarantine and Overwrite Protection: Decoders MUST write reconstructed data to an isolated temporary quarantine file and promote it via atomic rename only after Anchor Hash (and optional Bit 3 origin tag) verification succeeds. Implementations MUST NOT overwrite existing target files unless explicitly authorized by the operator, and MUST reject identical source and destination paths.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests registration of the media type application/elp8 in the IANA "Media Types" registry:

ul.li: Security considerations: See Section 5 of this document.
Interoperability considerations: Big-endian network byte order for all header fields.
Applications that use this media type: EULNO compression tools and archival utilities.
